20: #define PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD 0x5u
21: #define PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD 0x7u
22: #define PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD 0x8u
23: #define PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD 0x9u
24: #define PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD 0xau
25: #define PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1 11u
26: #define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON 0u
27: #define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF 1u
28: #define PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT 0u
29: #define PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH 1u
30: #define PM_QUEUE_DEPTH 8u
31: #define PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS 500u
32: #define PM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS 1000u

34: struct pwc_message
35: {
36:   uint32_t header;
37:   uint32_t param1;
38:   uint32_t param2;
39:   uint32_t param3;
40: };
41: 
42: static struct pwc_message g_queue[PM_QUEUE_DEPTH];
43: static volatile unsigned int g_head;
44: static volatile unsigned int g_tail;
45: static sem_t g_pwc_sem;
46: static sem_t g_worker_sem;
47: static sem_t g_psram_power_sem;
48: static volatile bool g_worker_ready;
49: static volatile bool g_ready_sent;
50: static volatile bool g_psram_power_waiting;
51: static volatile uint32_t g_psram_power_state;
52: static volatile int32_t g_psram_power_result;

55: static int ipc_heartbeat_worker(int argc, char **argv)
56: {
57:   static uint32_t heartbeat_payload;
58: 
59:   (void)argc;
60:   (void)argv;
61:   for (;;)
62:     {
63:       nxsig_usleep(2000000);
64:       (void)bk7258_mbox_send_message(2, 0x10,
65:                                      (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&heartbeat_payload,
66:                                      sizeof(heartbeat_payload), 0);
67:     }
68:   return 0;
69: }
70: 
71: static void pwc_rx(const void *raw)
72: {
73:   const uint8_t *bytes = raw;
74:   struct pwc_message message;
75:   unsigned int next = (g_head + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
76:   if (next == g_tail || bytes == NULL)
77:     {
78:       return;
79:     }
80:   message.header = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[0];
81:   message.param1 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[1];
82:   message.param2 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[2];
83:   message.param3 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[3];
84:   g_queue[g_head] = message;
85:   g_head = next;
86:   nxsem_post(&g_pwc_sem);
87: }
88: 
89: static int pwc_worker(int argc, char **argv)
90: {
91:   (void)argc;
92:   (void)argv;
93:   g_worker_ready = true;
94:   nxsem_post(&g_worker_sem);
95:   for (;;)
96:     {
97:       struct pwc_message message;
98:       nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&g_pwc_sem);
99:       message = g_queue[g_tail];
100:       g_tail = (g_tail + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
101:       /* Hardware power/clock actions stay in this thread, never in IRQ. */
102:       switch (message.header & 0xffu)
103:         {
104:           case PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD:
105:             /* param1 retains the vendor ON/OFF response. Extended CP
106:              * firmware returns the real vote result and detected capacity
107:              * in param2 and param3.
108:              */
109: 
110:             g_psram_power_state = message.param1;
111:             g_psram_power_result = (int32_t)message.param2;
112:             g_psram_capacity = message.param3;
113:             if (g_psram_power_waiting)
114:               {
115:                 g_psram_power_waiting = false;
116:                 nxsem_post(&g_psram_power_sem);
117:               }
118:             break;
119: 
120: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
121:           case PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD:
122:             if (message.param1 == 0u)
123:               {
124:                 (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
125:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
126:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
127:                   bk7258_psram_heap_used(), 0);
128:               }
129:             else if (message.param1 == PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF)
130:               {
131:                 /* This CP notification is sent after physical power-down. */
132: 
133:                 bk7258_psram_power_lost();
134:               }
135:             break;
136: 
137:           case PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD:
138:             bk7258_psram_dump();
139:             break;
140: 
141:           case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
142:             {
143:               int ret = bk7258_psram_shutdown();
144: 
145:               (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
146:                 PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD, PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
147:                 ret == 0 ? PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH :
148:                            PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT, 0);
149:             }
150:             break;
151: #endif
152: 
153:           default:
154:             break;
155:         }
156:     }
157:   return 0;
158: }

160: int bk7258_pwc_start(void)
161: {
162:   int pid;
163:   int ret;
164: 
165:   nxsem_init(&g_pwc_sem, 0, 0);
166:   nxsem_init(&g_worker_sem, 0, 0);
167:   nxsem_init(&g_psram_power_sem, 0, 0);
168:   g_head = 0;
169:   g_tail = 0;
170:   g_worker_ready = false;
171:   g_ready_sent = false;
172:   g_psram_power_waiting = false;
173:   g_psram_power_state = PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF;
174:   g_psram_power_result = -EIO;
175:   g_psram_capacity = 0;
176:   pid = bk7258_mailbox_init();
177:   if (pid < 0)
178:     {
179:       return pid;
180:     }
181:   bk7258_mailbox_set_pwc_rx(pwc_rx);
182:   /* Match Armino mb_ipc_heartbeat: notify CPU0 before PM ready and keep the
183:    * CPU1 liveness indication independent from the PWC worker. */
184:   if (bk7258_mbox_send_message(1, 0x10, 0, 0, 0) != 0)
185:     {
186:       return -1;
187:     }
188: 
189:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_hw_control(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
190:   if (ret < 0)
191:     {
192:       printf("PWC: IPC power-up transport timeout, error=%d\n", ret);
193:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
194:       return ret;
195:     }
196:   printf("PWC: IPC power-up transport complete\n");
197: 
198:   if (kthread_create("ipc-heartbeat", 100, 1536, ipc_heartbeat_worker,
199:                      NULL) < 0)
200:     {
201:       return -1;
202:     }
203:   pid = kthread_create("pwc", 110, 2048, pwc_worker, NULL);
204:   if (pid < 0)
205:     {
206:       return pid;
207:     }
208:   if (nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_worker_sem, MSEC2TICK(200)) < 0 ||
209:       !g_worker_ready)
210:     {
211:       printf("PWC: worker start timeout\n");
212:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
213:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
214:     }
215:   printf("PWC: worker ready\n");
216: 
217:   /* CP boots CPU1 from its low-power worker and waits there for this ready
218:    * command. Send it before requesting PSRAM, whose vote is handled by that
219:    * same worker, otherwise the two cores deadlock waiting for each other.
220:    */
221: 
222:   g_ready_sent = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD,
223:                                          1, 0, 0) == 0;
224:   if (!g_ready_sent)
225:     {
226:       printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready queue failed\n");
227:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
228:       return -EIO;
229:     }
230: 
231:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
232:   if (ret < 0)
233:     {
234:       printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready transport timeout, error=%d\n", ret);
235:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
236:       return ret;
237:     }
238: 
239:   printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready acknowledged by CP transport\n");
240: 
241: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
242:   g_psram_power_waiting = true;
243:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,

245:                                 PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON, 0);

496: 		val = *((uint32_t *)(start_addr));

501: 			if (*(pb + i) == '\0') {
502: 				// Found end of existing string, append new data
503: 				for (j = i; j < PSRAM_BYTES_PER_WORD && *pd != '\0'; j++) {
504: 					*(pb + j) = *pd++;
505: 				}
506: 				
507: 				// If we've reached the end of the input string, add null terminator
508: 				if (*pd == '\0' && j < PSRAM_BYTES_PER_WORD) {
509: 					*(pb + j) = '\0';
510: 				}
511: 				
512: 				*((uint32_t *)(start_addr)) = val;
513: 				
514: 				if (*pd == '\0') {
515: 					return start_addr;
516: 				}
517: 				break;
518: 			}
519: 		}
520: 		
521: 		// If no null terminator found in this word, move to next word
522: 		if (i == PSRAM_BYTES_PER_WORD) {
523: 			start_addr += PSRAM_BYTES_PER_WORD;
524: 		}
525: 		
526: 	} while (*pd != '\0');

327: static void pm_module_bootup_cpu1(pm_power_module_name_e module)
328: {
329: 	uint64_t previous_tick = 0;
330: 	uint64_t current_tick   = 0;
331: 	if(PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF == sys_drv_module_power_state_get(module))
332: 	{
333: 		if(module == PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1)
334: 		{
335: boot_cp1:
336: 			#if CONFIG_PM_AP_POWERDOWN_WHEN_LV
337: 			bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_CPU1, 0, 0);
338: 			#endif
339:             bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
340: 
341: 			#if defined(RECV_LOG_FROM_MBOX)
342: 			void reset_forward_log_status(void);
343: 			// reset cpu1's log transfer status on cpu0.
344: 			reset_forward_log_status();
345: 			#endif
346: 
347:             start_cpu1_core();
348: 
349: 			previous_tick = bk_aon_rtc_get_current_tick(AON_RTC_ID_1);
350: 			current_tick = previous_tick;
351: 			while((current_tick - previous_tick) < (PM_BOOT_CP1_WAITING_TIEM*AON_RTC_MS_TICK_CNT))
352: 			{
353: 				if (bk_pm_cp1_work_state_get()) // wait the cp1 response
354: 				{
355: 					break;
356: 				}
357: 				current_tick = bk_aon_rtc_get_current_tick(AON_RTC_ID_1);
358: 			}
359: 
360: 			if(!bk_pm_cp1_work_state_get())
361: 			{
362: 				BK_LOGD(NULL,"cp0 boot cp1[%d] time out, boot cp1 fail!!!\r\n",s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count);
363: 
364: 				/*Reset psram*/
365: 				bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MEDIA, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF);
366: 				bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MEDIA, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
367: 
368: 				s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count++;
369: 				if(s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count < PM_BOOT_CP1_TRY_COUNT)
370: 				{
371: 					goto boot_cp1;
372: 				}
373: 				if(s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count == PM_BOOT_CP1_TRY_COUNT)
374: 				{
375: 					#if CONFIG_WDT_EN
376: 					bk_wdt_force_reboot();//try 3 times, if fail ,reboot.
377: 					#endif
378: 				}
379: 			}
380: 		}
381: 	}
